raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Summary

Fixes #10255. The qwen3_5 swift backend dropped the assistant's `<think>...</think>` reasoning whenever the same assistant turn also carried `tool_calls`. The official `chat_template.jinja` (used by vLLM / transformers at inference) keeps it, so swift-trained models never saw "think, then call a tool" while being served in exactly that format — the train/infer mismatch behind #9234 (`</think><|im_end|>` / empty `<tool_call>` after SFT on Qwen3.5/3.6-35B-A3B).

## Root cause (from the issue report, confirmed on `main` @ dbc395ff02)

Two narrow mismatches with the jinja:

1. `swift/agent_template/qwen3_coder.py` — `Qwen3_5AgentTemplate._add_tool_call_prefix` used `pre_message['content']` only to decide on the `\n\n` separator and dropped the reasoning entirely. After the tool-call rebuild, the merged assistant turn had no `<think>` block at all.

2. `swift/template/base.py` — `_remove_history_thinking` and `_add_non_thinking_prefix` called `get_last_user_round(messages)` with the default `include_tool=True`. The official jinja uses the last **user** message as the boundary for stripping historical reasoning. With `tool` messages counted as a boundary, reasoning in the current agent round (which has tool messages between the user prompt and the assistant turn) was misclassified as history and stripped. `get_last_user_round` already accepts `include_tool` (from #9923); these two callers just needed to pass `include_tool=False`.

## Changes

- `swift/agent_template/qwen3_coder.py` — `_add_tool_call_prefix` now always preserves the preceding assistant content (so the `<think>` block survives the tool-call rebuild) and inserts the `\n\n` separator only when the effective (post-think) content is non-empty.
- `swift/template/base.py` — `_remove_history_thinking` and `_add_non_thinking_prefix` now pass `include_tool=False` to `get_last_user_round`, matching the official jinja boundary on the last user message.
- `tests/general/test_qwen3_5_agent_template.py` — new regression tests, CPU-only (no weights / tokenizer needed). Covers the three reasoning shapes (pure think, think + post-text, no think), the no-pre / non-assistant / empty-content edge cases, the `include_tool=False` boundary on `get_last_user_round`, and a static guard so a future refactor of the two call sites cannot silently regress.

## Verification

Ran a standalone verifier (`/tmp/verify_10255.py`) that exercises the new logic with hardcoded inputs against the patched source files. 18/18 checks pass, including a regression comparison that confirms the OLD behavior reproduces #10255 (drops reasoning) while the NEW behavior preserves it. The pytest suite itself runs in CI on this branch (this env doesn't have the heavy `swift` import chain satisfied).

## Related

- #10255 (this fix)
- #9234 (the user-visible symptom — same train/infer mismatch)
- #9923 (added `include_tool` to `get_last_user_round`; my fix uses it correctly)

nodes.body:
Thanks for picking this up. I tested this PR (head 3b2cb6f9) end-to-end with `template.encode` against the official jinja (tokenizer: Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-Base, 13 samples incl. the repro in #10255).

Token-exact matches vs jinja:

| version | last_round | all |
|---|---|---|
| main @ dbc395ff | 5/13 | 11/13 |
| this PR | 4/13 | 4/13 |

All 9 mismatches on this PR contain the reasoning twice. With the #10255 repro:

```
<think>\nI need to check the stock first.\n</think>\n\n<think>\nI need to check the stock first.\n</think>\n\n<tool_call>...
```

Cause: `_add_tool_call_prefix` now prepends `pre_message['content']`, but `pre_message` itself is not cleared, so the two assistant messages are merged and the reasoning appears twice. Clearing `pre_message['content']` alone is not enough: `_add_non_thinking_prefix` then adds `<think>\n\n</think>\n\n` to the now-empty first element. Also, `_remove_history_thinking` only strips `content[0]`, so reasoning in earlier rounds is not removed once content is a list.

The unit tests call `_add_tool_call_prefix` in isolation, so they don't catch this. An encode-level comparison against `tokenizer.apply_chat_template` would.

You're right — that's a real regression, and it is fixed in `0d75a91a`.

## Root cause

`_add_tool_call_prefix` (Qwen3.5/3.6) re-emits the preceding assistant content — reasoning included — before `<tool_call>`. But `_preprocess_tool_call` only replaced the `tool_call` block: the original assistant message stayed in the list as its own turn, and the merged turn carried the same content again. Every tool-call round therefore rendered the assistant content twice. On the #10255 repro the reasoning is in *both* copies, which matches your "all 9 mismatches contain the reasoning twice" table exactly.

Reproduced locally against `_preprocess_tool_call` before touching anything:

```
BEFORE the fix, AFTER _preprocess_tool_call:
  assistant: '<think>I should check the weather.</think>\nLet me look it up.'          <- 1st
  assistant: '<think>I should check the weather.</think>\nLet me look it up.\n\n<tool_call>...' <- 2nd (duplicate)
```

## The fix

A generic `_tool_call_prefix_absorbs_content(pre_message)` hook (`swift/agent_template/base.py`, default `False`). `Qwen3_5AgentTemplate` opts in **only when the prefix actually re-emits the content** — assistant role, non-empty string content — so the hook's answer can't drift from its own branch conditions. When set, `_preprocess_tool_call` replaces `[pre_message, tool_call...]` as one message and carries the pre_message's `loss`/`loss_scale` over when the tool_call block doesn't set them:

```
AFTER the fix:
  assistant: 'PHEreasoning</think>\nLet me look it up.\n\n<tool_call>\n<function=get_weather>...'   <- single turn
```

Templates whose prefix emits only a separator or channel token (DeepSeek v4, Kimi K3 — same hook) keep the preceding message as its own turn; a test pins that they're unaffected, along with `qwen3_coder`.

## Why this should also beat base on your table

Base renders reasoning and tool_call as **two** assistant turns; the official jinja emits one turn. Folding them into one removes that structural difference, which is what the 2 base-side mismatches in `last_round` were. The separator logic itself is unchanged (only when effective post-think text is non-empty).

## Validation

- `tests/general/test_qwen3_5_agent_template.py`: 14 passed (was 9); new cases cover render-once, pure-reasoning-without-separator, loss carry-over, prefix-only templates unaffected, and flag-vs-consumption consistency (incl. the non-string content case).
- `tests/general/test_deepseek_v41_template.py`, `test_glm4_5_agent_template.py`, `test_protocol_tool_choice.py` pass with the change.
- `test_template.py` has 3 failures in this sandbox (`addict` not installed / modelscope import), which fail identically on the unmodified branch — environmental, unrelated.
- yapf/isort/flake8 clean on the four touched files.

I could not re-run your exact 13-sample token-exact comparison here (no tokenizer download in this sandbox), so the strongest claim is mechanism-level: the duplicate copy is gone and the merged turn's shape now matches the jinja contract your harness computed against. If you can re-run your script on `0d75a91a`, that would settle the table.

Thanks — re-ran the same 13-sample token-exact comparison on `0d75a91a` (Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-Base tokenizer, `enable_thinking=True`, `preserve_thinking` default):

| | last_round | all |
|---|---|---|
| v4.5.3 | 5/13 | 11/13 |
| 0d75a91a | 13/13 | 11/13 |

The two remaining `all` mismatches (past-turn reasoning kept by swift, dropped by the jinja) are identical on v4.5.3 and come from the `preserve_thinking` default, not from this PR. `tests/general/test_qwen3_5_agent_template.py`: 14 passed.

On all 13 samples plus 15 edge cases, 0d75a91a renders exactly the same text as the alternative fix in RerankerGuo/ms-swift#1, so I'm closing that one in favour of this.

Thanks for the thorough re-verification — 13/13 on `last_round` and the closed alternative confirms the approach.

On the two remaining `all` mismatches: I agree they don't call for a change in this PR. They come from the `preserve_thinking` default (swift keeps past-turn reasoning in the encoded history), which is deliberate: in training, retaining earlier rounds' reasoning is what teaches the model *not* to re-derive it, whereas the official jinja is inference-oriented and strips it. As you showed, that behavior is identical on v4.5.3, so it predates this PR and this PR neither worsens nor masks it — `all` stays at the 11/13 baseline while the regression on the current turn is fixed.

Changing that default would alter rendering for every Qwen3.5/3.6 user, so if the mismatch ever needs reconciling it should be a separate, maintainer-endorsed change to the `preserve_thinking` semantics rather than a rider on this fix. Happy to open a tracking issue if the maintainers want one.

+# Copyright (c) ModelScope Contributors. All rights reserved.
+"""Regression tests for #10255.
+
+The Qwen3.5/3.6 swift backend was dropping the assistant's ``<think>...</think>``
+reasoning whenever the same assistant turn also carried ``tool_calls`` (and, in
+the history-thinking path, whenever a tool message sat between the user prompt
+and the assistant reasoning). The official ``chat_template.jinja`` (used by
+vLLM / transformers at inference) keeps both, which is the root cause of the
+train/infer mismatch on Qwen3.5/3.6 agent data (the same upstream issue as
+#9234 — ``</think><|im_end|>`` / empty ``<tool_call>`` after SFT).
+
+These tests exercise the agent-template and template-base hooks directly,
+without loading a model or downloading tokenizer files, so they run on CPU
+only.
+"""
+import json
+import unittest
+
+from swift.agent_template import agent_template_map
+from swift.template.base import Template
+from swift.template.utils import get_last_user_round
+
+
+class TestQwen3_5AddToolCallPrefix(unittest.TestCase):
+    """The Qwen3.5/3.6 jinja keeps the preceding assistant ``content`` (including
+    ``<think>...</think>`` reasoning) before ``<tool_call>`` and only inserts
+    ``\\n\\n`` between them when the effective (post-think) content is
+    non-empty. The previous swift implementation used ``pre_message['content']``
+    only to decide on the separator and dropped the reasoning entirely — see
+    #10255.
+    """
+
+    def setUp(self):
+        self.tpl = agent_template_map['qwen3_5']()
+        self.tool_call_msg = {
+            'role': 'tool_call',
+            'content': json.dumps({
+                'name': 'search',
+                'arguments': {
+                    'query': 'stock'
+                },
+            }),
+        }
+        self.tool_content = self.tpl._format_tool_calls([self.tool_call_msg])
+
+    def test_think_plus_post_text_then_tool_call_keeps_thinking_and_separator(self):
+        pre = {
+            'role': 'assistant',
+            'content': '<think>\nI need to check the stock first.\n</think>\n\n',
+        }
+        out = self.tpl._add_tool_call_prefix(self.tool_content, pre)
+        # Reasoning must be preserved verbatim (this was the regression).
+        self.assertIn('<think>\nI need to check the stock first.\n</think>', out)
+        # Effective content after </think> is empty here, but the original
+        # content ends in '\n\n' so we still want the <tool_call> to follow it
+        # without an extra blank line inserted by the prefix hook.
+        self.assertTrue(out.startswith(pre['content']))
+        # The tool_call block must follow.
+        self.assertTrue(out.endswith(self.tool_content))
+
+    def test_pure_thinking_then_tool_call_keeps_thinking_without_extra_separator(self):
+        pre = {
+            'role': 'assistant',
+            'content': '<think>\nonly thinking, no post-text\n</think>',
+        }
+        out = self.tpl._add_tool_call_prefix(self.tool_content, pre)
+        # Reasoning preserved.
+        self.assertIn('only thinking, no post-text', out)
+        # No inserted '\\n\\n' separator between </think> and <tool_call> when
+        # there is no post-think text — the jinja template just concatenates.
+        self.assertNotIn('</think>\n\n<tool_call>', out)
+        self.assertTrue(out.endswith('</think>' + self.tool_content))
+
+    def test_think_plus_post_text_then_tool_call_inserts_separator(self):
+        pre = {
+            'role': 'assistant',
+            'content': '<think>\nplan\n</think>\nSome preamble text.',
+        }
+        out = self.tpl._add_tool_call_prefix(self.tool_content, pre)
+        # Reasoning preserved.
+        self.assertIn('plan', out)
+        # Separator before tool_call when effective content is non-empty.
+        self.assertIn('Some preamble text.\n\n<tool_call>', out)
+
+    def test_no_pre_message_returns_tool_content_unchanged(self):
+        out = self.tpl._add_tool_call_prefix(self.tool_content, None)
+        self.assertEqual(out, self.tool_content)
+
+    def test_non_assistant_pre_message_returns_tool_content_unchanged(self):
+        out = self.tpl._add_tool_call_prefix(self.tool_content, {
+            'role': 'user',
+            'content': 'no preceding assistant here',
+        })
+        self.assertEqual(out, self.tool_content)
+
+    def test_empty_string_content_returns_tool_content_unchanged(self):
+        out = self.tpl._add_tool_call_prefix(self.tool_content, {
+            'role': 'assistant',
+            'content': '',
+        })
+        self.assertEqual(out, self.tool_content)
+
+
+class TestGetLastUserRoundIncludeTool(unittest.TestCase):
+    """`_remove_history_thinking` and `_add_non_thinking_prefix` in
+    ``swift.template.base`` must use the last *user* message as the boundary
+    for stripping historical reasoning (not the last user-or-tool), to match
+    the official Qwen3.5/3.6 chat_template.jinja. The function accepts an
+    ``include_tool`` keyword since #9923; #10255 fixes the two call sites.
+    """
+
+    def test_include_tool_false_ignores_tool_messages(self):
+        messages = [
+            {
+                'role': 'user',
+                'content': 'first user'
+            },
+            {
+                'role': 'assistant',
+                'content': 'first assistant'
+            },
+            {
+                'role': 'tool',
+                'content': 'tool result'
+            },
+            {
+                'role': 'assistant',
+                'content': 'second assistant'
+            },
+        ]
+        self.assertEqual(get_last_user_round(messages, include_tool=False), 0)
+        self.assertEqual(get_last_user_round(messages, include_tool=True), 2)
+
+    def test_include_tool_false_matches_first_user(self):
+        messages = [
+            {
+                'role': 'user',
+                'content': 'only user'
+            },
+            {
+                'role': 'assistant',
+                'content': 'a1'
+            },
+            {
+                'role': 'tool',
+                'content': 't1'
+            },
+            {
+                'role': 'assistant',
+                'content': 'a2'
+            },
+            {
+                'role': 'tool',
+                'content': 't2'
+            },
+            {
+                'role': 'assistant',
+                'content': 'a3'
+            },
+        ]
+        # The last user message is at index 0; everything from index 1
+        # onward (including all tool messages and assistants after them)
+        # belongs to the current round, so reasoning there must be
+        # preserved by `_remove_history_thinking`.
+        self.assertEqual(get_last_user_round(messages, include_tool=False), 0)
+
+    def test_template_history_thinking_calls_use_include_tool_false(self):
+        """Static guard so a future refactor of the two call sites cannot
+        silently regress to the old (include_tool=True default) behaviour."""
+        import inspect
+        for name in ('_remove_history_thinking', '_add_non_thinking_prefix'):
+            method = getattr(Template, name)
+            source = inspect.getsource(method)
+            self.assertIn(
+                'get_last_user_round(messages, include_tool=False)',
+                source,
+                msg=(f'{name} must call '
+                     '`get_last_user_round(messages, include_tool=False)` '
+                     'to match the official jinja boundary; #10255'),
+            )
+
+
+class TestQwen3_5ToolCallMergesPreAssistant(unittest.TestCase):
+    """`_preprocess_tool_call` must fold the preceding assistant message into
+    the merged tool_call turn when the prefix re-emits its content (#10259).
+
+    Leaving both in place renders the assistant content — reasoning
+    included — twice, which is what the upstream reviewer measured against
+    the official jinja (9 of 13 samples mismatched, all with the reasoning
+    duplicated). Templates whose prefix emits only a separator or a channel
+    token must keep the preceding message as its own turn.
+    """
+
+    def setUp(self):
+        self.tpl = agent_template_map['qwen3_5']()
+
+    def _run(self, messages, template_name='qwen3_5', pre=None):
+        import swift.template.base as base
+        agent = agent_template_map[template_name]()
+
+        class _Inputs:
+            pass
+
+        inputs = _Inputs()
+        inputs.tools = None
+        inputs.messages = [dict(m) for m in messages]
+        shim = Template.__new__(Template)
+        shim._agent_template = template_name
+        shim._agent_template_cache = {template_name: agent}
+        shim.template_meta = None
+        agent.template_meta = None
+        shim._preprocess_tool_call(inputs)
+        return inputs.messages
+
+    def _tool_call_msg(self):
+        return {
+            'role': 'tool_call',
+            'content': json.dumps({
+                'name': 'search',
+                'arguments': {
+                    'query': 'stock'
+                },
+            }),
+        }
+
+    def test_think_and_tool_call_render_assistant_content_once(self):
+        reasoning = '<think>\nCheck the stock quote first.\n</think>\n\nLet me look it up.'
+        messages = [{
+            'role': 'user',
+            'content': 'How is NVDA?'
+        }, {
+            'role': 'assistant',
+            'content': reasoning
+        },
+                    self._tool_call_msg(), {
+                        'role': 'tool',
+                        'content': 'NVDA +2%'
+                    }, {
+                        'role': 'assistant',
+                        'content': 'NVDA is up 2 percent.'
+                    }]
+
+        out = self._run(messages)
+
+        roles = [m['role'] for m in out]
+        self.assertEqual(len(out), 4, msg=f'expected user + merged assistant + tool + answer, got {roles}')
+        merged = out[1]
+        self.assertEqual(merged['role'], 'assistant')
+        count = merged['content'].count(reasoning)
+        self.assertEqual(
+            count,
+            1,
+            msg=(f'assistant content (with reasoning) must render exactly once; got '
+                 f'{count} occurrences: {merged["content"]!r}'),
+        )
+        self.assertIn('<tool_call>', merged['content'])
+        # The separator stays when effective post-think text exists.
+        self.assertIn('\n\n<tool_call>', merged['content'])
+        # The reasoning lands before the tool call, matching the jinja.
+        self.assertLess(merged['content'].index(reasoning), merged['content'].index('<tool_call>'))
+
+    def test_pure_reasoning_turn_keeps_reasoning_without_separator(self):
+        reasoning = '<think>\nThe input is complete; call the tool directly.\n</think>'
+        messages = [{
+            'role': 'user',
+            'content': 'Search the stock'
+        }, {
+            'role': 'assistant',
+            'content': reasoning
+        },
+                    self._tool_call_msg()]
+
+        out = self._run(messages)
+
+        self.assertEqual([m['role'] for m in out], ['user', 'assistant'])
+        self.assertEqual(out[1]['content'].count(reasoning), 1)
+        self.assertIn('<tool_call>', out[1]['content'])
+        self.assertNotIn(
+            '\n\n<tool_call>',
+            out[1]['content'],
+            msg='a pure-reasoning turn emits the tool_call directly after, without \\n\\n',
+        )
+
+    def test_absorbed_pre_message_loss_fields_carry_over(self):
+        messages = [{
+            'role': 'user',
+            'content': 'Search'
+        }, {
+            'role': 'assistant',
+            'content': 'Let me search.',
+            'loss': 1,
+            'loss_scale': 'default'
+        },
+                    self._tool_call_msg(), {
+                        'role': 'tool',
+                        'content': 'NVDA +2%'
+                    }]
+
+        out = self._run(messages)
+
+        merged = out[1]
+        self.assertEqual(len(out), 3)
+        self.assertEqual(merged.get('loss'), 1, msg='the folded assistant turn keeps its own loss field')
+        self.assertEqual(merged.get('loss_scale'), 'default')
+
+    def test_prefix_only_templates_keep_pre_message_as_own_turn(self):
+        for name in ('deepseek_v4', 'kimi_k3'):
+            messages = [{
+                'role': 'user',
+                'content': 'Search'
+            }, {
+                'role': 'assistant',
+                'content': 'Let me search.'
+            },
+                        self._tool_call_msg(), {
+                            'role': 'tool',
+                            'content': 'NVDA +2%'
+                        }]
+
+            out = self._run(messages, template_name=name)
+
+            self.assertEqual(
+                [m['role'] for m in out],
+                ['user', 'assistant', 'assistant', 'tool'],
+                msg=(f'{name} uses a prefix-only hook: the preceding assistant message must '
+                     'survive as its own turn'),
+            )
+            self.assertNotEqual(
+                out[1]['content'],
+                out[2]['content'],
+                msg=f'{name} must not duplicate the assistant content into the tool turn',
+            )
+
+    def test_absorbs_flag_matches_prefix_consumption(self):
+        template = agent_template_map['qwen3_5']()
+        cases = [
+            (None, False),
+            ({
+                'role': 'user',
+                'content': 'hi'
+            }, False),
+            ({
+                'role': 'assistant',
+                'content': ''
+            }, False),
+            ({
+                'role': 'assistant',
+                'content': 'text'
+            }, True),
+            ({
+                'role': 'assistant',
+                'content': ['not', 'a', 'string']
+            }, False),
+        ]
+        for pre_message, expected in cases:
+            with self.subTest(pre_message=pre_message):
+                self.assertEqual(template._tool_call_prefix_absorbs_content(pre_message), expected)
+        # The graft is generic; only qwen3_5 opts in on these templates.
+        for name in ('deepseek_v4', 'kimi_k3', 'qwen3_coder'):
+            agent = agent_template_map[name]()
+            self.assertFalse(
+                agent._tool_call_prefix_absorbs_content({
+                    'role': 'assistant',
+                    'content': 'text'
+                }),
+                msg=f'{name} must keep the default (no absorption)',
+            )
+
+
+if __name__ == '__main__':
+    unittest.main()

issue_comments.body:
Thanks for picking this up. I tested this PR (head 3b2cb6f9) end-to-end with `template.encode` against the official jinja (tokenizer: Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-Base, 13 samples incl. the repro in #10255).

Token-exact matches vs jinja:

| version | last_round | all |
|---|---|---|
| main @ dbc395ff | 5/13 | 11/13 |
| this PR | 4/13 | 4/13 |

All 9 mismatches on this PR contain the reasoning twice. With the #10255 repro:

```
<think>\nI need to check the stock first.\n</think>\n\n<think>\nI need to check the stock first.\n</think>\n\n<tool_call>...
```

Cause: `_add_tool_call_prefix` now prepends `pre_message['content']`, but `pre_message` itself is not cleared, so the two assistant messages are merged and the reasoning appears twice. Clearing `pre_message['content']` alone is not enough: `_add_non_thinking_prefix` then adds `<think>\n\n</think>\n\n` to the now-empty first element. Also, `_remove_history_thinking` only strips `content[0]`, so reasoning in earlier rounds is not removed once content is a list.

The unit tests call `_add_tool_call_prefix` in isolation, so they don't catch this. An encode-level comparison against `tokenizer.apply_chat_template` would.

You're right — that's a real regression, and it is fixed in `0d75a91a`.

## Root cause

`_add_tool_call_prefix` (Qwen3.5/3.6) re-emits the preceding assistant content — reasoning included — before `<tool_call>`. But `_preprocess_tool_call` only replaced the `tool_call` block: the original assistant message stayed in the list as its own turn, and the merged turn carried the same content again. Every tool-call round therefore rendered the assistant content twice. On the #10255 repro the reasoning is in *both* copies, which matches your "all 9 mismatches contain the reasoning twice" table exactly.

Reproduced locally against `_preprocess_tool_call` before touching anything:

```
BEFORE the fix, AFTER _preprocess_tool_call:
  assistant: '<think>I should check the weather.</think>\nLet me look it up.'          <- 1st
  assistant: '<think>I should check the weather.</think>\nLet me look it up.\n\n<tool_call>...' <- 2nd (duplicate)
```

## The fix

A generic `_tool_call_prefix_absorbs_content(pre_message)` hook (`swift/agent_template/base.py`, default `False`). `Qwen3_5AgentTemplate` opts in **only when the prefix actually re-emits the content** — assistant role, non-empty string content — so the hook's answer can't drift from its own branch conditions. When set, `_preprocess_tool_call` replaces `[pre_message, tool_call...]` as one message and carries the pre_message's `loss`/`loss_scale` over when the tool_call block doesn't set them:

```
AFTER the fix:
  assistant: 'PHEreasoning</think>\nLet me look it up.\n\n<tool_call>\n<function=get_weather>...'   <- single turn
```

Templates whose prefix emits only a separator or channel token (DeepSeek v4, Kimi K3 — same hook) keep the preceding message as its own turn; a test pins that they're unaffected, along with `qwen3_coder`.

## Why this should also beat base on your table

Base renders reasoning and tool_call as **two** assistant turns; the official jinja emits one turn. Folding them into one removes that structural difference, which is what the 2 base-side mismatches in `last_round` were. The separator logic itself is unchanged (only when effective post-think text is non-empty).

## Validation

- `tests/general/test_qwen3_5_agent_template.py`: 14 passed (was 9); new cases cover render-once, pure-reasoning-without-separator, loss carry-over, prefix-only templates unaffected, and flag-vs-consumption consistency (incl. the non-string content case).
- `tests/general/test_deepseek_v41_template.py`, `test_glm4_5_agent_template.py`, `test_protocol_tool_choice.py` pass with the change.
- `test_template.py` has 3 failures in this sandbox (`addict` not installed / modelscope import), which fail identically on the unmodified branch — environmental, unrelated.
- yapf/isort/flake8 clean on the four touched files.

I could not re-run your exact 13-sample token-exact comparison here (no tokenizer download in this sandbox), so the strongest claim is mechanism-level: the duplicate copy is gone and the merged turn's shape now matches the jinja contract your harness computed against. If you can re-run your script on `0d75a91a`, that would settle the table.

Thanks — re-ran the same 13-sample token-exact comparison on `0d75a91a` (Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-Base tokenizer, `enable_thinking=True`, `preserve_thinking` default):

| | last_round | all |
|---|---|---|
| v4.5.3 | 5/13 | 11/13 |
| 0d75a91a | 13/13 | 11/13 |

The two remaining `all` mismatches (past-turn reasoning kept by swift, dropped by the jinja) are identical on v4.5.3 and come from the `preserve_thinking` default, not from this PR. `tests/general/test_qwen3_5_agent_template.py`: 14 passed.

On all 13 samples plus 15 edge cases, 0d75a91a renders exactly the same text as the alternative fix in RerankerGuo/ms-swift#1, so I'm closing that one in favour of this.

Thanks for the thorough re-verification — 13/13 on `last_round` and the closed alternative confirms the approach.

On the two remaining `all` mismatches: I agree they don't call for a change in this PR. They come from the `preserve_thinking` default (swift keeps past-turn reasoning in the encoded history), which is deliberate: in training, retaining earlier rounds' reasoning is what teaches the model *not* to re-derive it, whereas the official jinja is inference-oriented and strips it. As you showed, that behavior is identical on v4.5.3, so it predates this PR and this PR neither worsens nor masks it — `all` stays at the 11/13 baseline while the regression on the current turn is fixed.

Changing that default would alter rendering for every Qwen3.5/3.6 user, so if the mismatch ever needs reconciling it should be a separate, maintainer-endorsed change to the `preserve_thinking` semantics rather than a rider on this fix. Happy to open a tracking issue if the maintainers want one.
